newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ shares bounce to end in positive territory.
newsitem.headline: NZ shares bounce to end in positive territory.

text.p: New Zealand shares bounced off their lows to end in positive territory on Thursday thanks to strength in Telecom and a recovery from early weakness in forestry stocks.
The NZSE-40 capital index ended 2.64 points stronger at 2,393.92, well off its low of 2,381.25.
"The tone remains pretty strong," said Jim Patterson at First NZ Capital.
Peter Lynds at ANZ Securities said it was still a waiting market, with news of a government coalition expected within the next week.
But Telecom, Fletcher Paper and Carter Holt Harvey all showed strength, the latter handing back only four cents of Wednesday's 18 cent rise.
The announcement of a $313 million upgrade at Carter's Kinleith pulp and paper mill to increase total production by 30 percent was in line with the market's expectations.
Elsewhere, Air New Zealand "A" and "B" shares were each up five cents, while Fletcher Energy showed continued weakness after disappointing drilling reports.
The total volume of NZ$76.8 million included a portfolio reported overnight totalling $17 million, which covered a wide range of leading stocks.
